description: The pie chart represents the distribution of mathematical topics across various categories. The chart is divided into 11 slices, each representing a distinct topic. The slices are labeled with their corresponding topics and percentages, and are colored differently for visual distinction. The largest slice, colored blue, represents "Algebra - Olympiad-level" and accounts for approximately 21.19% of the total. The second-largest slice, colored pink, represents "Algebra - High School" and accounts for around 17.83%. Other notable slices include "Pre-Calculus - High School" (brown, 14.21%), "Combinatorics - Olympiad-level" (green, 9.56%), and "Linear Algebra and Abstract Algebra - University-level" (purple, 6.46%). The remaining slices represent various other mathematical topics, including "Geometry - Olympiad-level" (orange, 6.46%), "Calculus and Analysis - University-level" (light blue, 6.20%), "Probability - University-level" (teal, 5.43%), "Statistics - University-level" (yellow, 4.39%), "Geometry - High School" (gray, 3.62%), and "Differential Equations - University-level" (pinkish-gray, 3.62%), and "Olympiad-level" (light gray, 1.03%). The chart does not include a legend, but the labels are placed outside the chart, connected to their corresponding slices by lines. The slices are not visually emphasized or ordered in a particular way.
